In Whitby Estates, West Vancouver, the 55+ homes you can buy are OUT OF AREA, OUT OF AREA and OUT OF AREA (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is rental, retirement residence or care and subsidized rental. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Whitby Estates
OUT OF AREA — Westview Terrace — 1390 Duchess Ave (Ambleside)

The nearest known 55+ strata to buy. A current listing describes "a quiet, well-kept 25-unit concrete building (55+)" in the heart of Ambleside; the North Shore guide also lists it among West Vancouver buildings that "all have a 55+ bylaw."
OUT OF AREA — Tudor Gardens — 843 22nd St (Ambleside/Dundarave edge)
Built 1992; a current listing states "55+ age restriction, no pets," and building data records age restrictions.
OUT OF AREA — Lincoln Gardens — 2110 Marine Dr (Ambleside)

Built 1988, 44 units. The North Shore guide lists it as a 55+ bylaw building; building data records "Age restrictions" without stating the age — the 55+ figure rests on the guide, so confirm on the Form B.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Whitby Estates (not for sale)

items.t: In Whitby Estates: none: No purpose-built seniors rental building of any kind exists in the pocket; the housing stock is detached freehold houses plus the two general-market strata pockets below.

OUT OF AREA — Westerleigh PARC — 725 22nd St (Ambleside/Dundarave edge): PARC Retirement Living's independent-living rental residence at 22nd and Marine Drive, LEED Gold certified, meals, fitness programs and transportation included. Rental only — nothing to buy.

In Whitby Estates: none: No retirement residence, assisted-living residence or care home is registered or marketed at any address in the pocket; the Assisted Living Registry's complete West Vancouver list is the four addresses in the checks above, all outside the pocket.

OUT OF AREA — Amica West Vancouver — 659 Clyde Ave (Ambleside east end, by Taylor Way; the closest care residence to Whitby Estates): Independent living, registered assisted living suites and long-term care in one rental residence; registered in the Assisted Living Registry (class SN), operator WC Operating (Ivy BC) GP Inc.

OUT OF AREA — Amica Lions Gate — 701 Keith Rd (Park Royal side): Independent living, assisted living and long-term care suites; registered in the Assisted Living Registry (class SN) at 701–721 Keith Road, operator WC Operating (Ivy BC) GP Inc.

OUT OF AREA — Hollyburn House (Venvi Hollyburn House) — 2095 Marine Dr (Ambleside): Independent living, assisted living, residential care, short-term and respite stays, operated by Cogir Senior Living; registered in the Assisted Living Registry (class SN), legal operator WC Operating (British Columbia - 1) GP Inc.

OUT OF AREA — Inglewood Care Centre — 725 Inglewood Ave (Ambleside): Long-term care, 230 publicly funded beds, opened 1979, operated by the Baptist Housing Society (not-for-profit); access through Vancouver Coastal Health.
In Whitby Estates: none: No non-profit or income-based seniors building exists in the pocket, and none appears for it in the BC Housing Zone 1 directory.
OUT OF AREA — Kiwanis Manor — 959 21st St (Ambleside): is the District's known non-profit below-market seniors rental (Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society; applications year-round).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Whitby Estates

items.t: Whitby Estates is a small, defined subdivision pocket inside the Chartwell neighbourhood of the British Properties, District of West Vancouver, on the slope above Taylor Way. Its streets include Whitby Road, Folkestone Way, Kadlec Court, Garden Court and Highgrove Mews.

MLS sub-area name as the board (Greater Vancouver REALTORS®) uses it: Whitby Estates. Overlap to know about: some Whitby Road homes are also marketed under the neighbouring Chartwell sub-area name, so searches should cover both names.
Nearby areas: Chartwell (surrounding), Chelsea Park (south), Westhill and Canterbury (west), and the Taylor Way corridor (east).

The District's OCP treats the British Properties as an established existing neighbourhood within its "individual, unique neighbourhoods" structure; growth is directed to the town and village centres (Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild, Horseshoe Bay), not into the Properties.

Schools: the catchment pair sits on Chartwell Drive — Chartwell Elementary (K–7, 1300 Chartwell Drive), which West Vancouver Schools describes as situated in the British Properties overlooking Vancouver and Burrard Inlet, and Sentinel Secondary (Grades 8–12, 1250 Chartwell Drive) next door. Confirm catchments by exact address with West Vancouver Schools.

Transit: no frequent transit runs into the Estates themselves; the nearest major service is at Park Royal Exchange (R2 RapidBus one-seat to Lonsdale Quay, Phibbs Exchange and Metrotown since September 7, 2026, plus Blue Bus routes) via Taylor Way.
The hospital for the District is Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver (Vancouver Coastal Health) — there is no hospital in West Vancouver.

Where 55+ housing actually concentrates in West Vancouver: none of it is here. Every known seniors building in the District is in Ambleside (with one care residence on the Park Royal side). The District's own seniors hub, the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street, is also in Ambleside.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Whitby Estates

items.t: Framing, stated honestly: the strata age-bylaw rules below are general BC law. They do not attach to anything in Whitby Estates today — the pocket has no 55+ strata, and its two strata complexes (Garden Court, Highgrove) have no known age bylaw. They matter to a Whitby Estates buyer in two ways: they govern the Ambleside 55+ buildings in if the buyer redirects there, and they are the rules any BC strata the buyer considers will live under.

Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: is the District of West Vancouver's zoning bylaw (District bylaw page, number 4662). Houses sit in the RS single-family dwelling zones in Section 200, which set minimum site areas from 488 m² in RS5 to 8,094 m² in RS1 and list secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among the permitted uses in the single-family zones — the bylaw basis for the large-lot pattern of the British Properties and for adding a suite to a Whitby Estates house. Do not publish 2506 / 2220 for West Vancouver.

OCP: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018: The OCP treats the British Properties as an established existing neighbourhood and directs growth to the town and village centres, not into the Properties — which is why no seniors-density product is planned for this hillside under the current plan.
Building scheme on top of District rules: Confirm the Whitby Estates subdivision's specific covenant set per property, on title.

Development permits on this slope: a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit applies to work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface, and an Environmental Development Permit applies within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank — both live issues on Whitby Estates lots backing onto forest or creeks.

Additional school tax: the Province's additional school tax applies at Whitby Estates price points — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

Care is not a strata product: the Ambleside residences here are registered with BC's Assisted Living Registry, and publicly funded long-term care (Inglewood's 230 beds) is allocated through Vancouver Coastal Health after an assessment — neither is bought, and neither uses a strata age bylaw.

blocks.text: Good to know about Whitby Estates

items.t: The same house can be listed under two sub-area names. Some Whitby Road homes are marketed under Chartwell and others under Whitby Estates, so a comp set or a saved search built on one name only will miss real Whitby Estates sales. Search both names, plus street searches on Whitby Road, Folkestone Way and Chartwell Drive.

There is a second approval office nobody expects. On top of District permits, any new build, extension, alteration, fence or structure in a British Properties subdivision needs plan approval from British Pacific Properties Limited under the restrictive covenants registered on title — and the covenant set differs by subdivision. A downsizer planning a main-floor addition or a caregiver suite should budget time for that step, not just the District's.

All of the District's seniors infrastructure sits on one flat corridor. The four Assisted Living Registry entries, the long-term care home, all three 55+ strata buildings, the Community Centre and Aquatic Centre (2121 Marine Drive), the Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive) and the Seniors' Activity Centre (695 21st Street) are all within the Ambleside flat or its edges. The hillside — Whitby Estates included — has no registered seniors housing at all, which is the single most useful fact a 55+ buyer searching this pocket can be told up front.

The District's seniors centre is geared to exactly this buyer — but it is in Ambleside. The District describes the Seniors' Activity Centre as "home to many programs, services, and amenities geared toward 55+ adults," including the Garden Side Bistro, the SACS on 21st shop, rehabilitation, fitness, arts, learning and computer programs, and its Seniors' Services page lists a shuttle bus service and phone-in food delivery for West Vancouver residents. A Whitby Estates senior uses these by driving (or being driven) down to 21st Street — nothing equivalent exists up the hill.

"Garden Court condos" are eight townhome-style residences, not a condo building. Aerie at 2575 Garden Court is an 8-residence concrete-and-stone strata by British Pacific Properties (strata plan BCS3645, built 2010), with geothermal heating and private two-car garages; listings describe two-level townhome layouts. Buyers picturing elevator-condo downsizing should read the actual layouts before assuming single-level living.

The District's biggest future seniors supply is also in Ambleside, not here. The Inglewood Campus of Care redevelopment (District approval September 21, 2026) rebuilds Inglewood Care Centre at 364 long-term care beds in Phase 1, then adds 200 independent living units and 161 seniors rental units in Phase 2 — future West Vancouver seniors supply, all on the Ambleside site, with wait lists run through Baptist Housing, not the District.
There are no published market stats for this pocket to quote.

The additional school tax is a routine line item at these values. At Whitby Estates price points the Province's additional school tax (0.2% on the residential portion between $3 million and $4 million, 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027) applies on top of District property taxes — worth surfacing in a buyer's first-year cost picture, not discovering at tax time.

faq.a: No — none of any tenure. The Assisted Living Registry's West Vancouver list has four residences, all in Ambleside or by Park Royal; the North Shore guide to 55+ bylaw buildings lists three, all in Ambleside. A "Whitby Estates 55+" search is really a search for detached houses and two general-market strata pockets.
faq.q: Is there any 55+ housing in Whitby Estates itself?

faq.a: An ordinary home with no age rules attached: a detached freehold estate house on a large lot, or a unit in one of the two small strata pockets — Aerie at Garden Court (8 residences, built 2010) or Highgrove (18 townhomes, built 2013). Downsizing into the strata pockets trades the house-maintenance load for strata living, but the homes themselves are large, multi-level view homes, not single-level seniors product.
faq.q: So what does a 55+ buyer actually buy in Whitby Estates?

faq.a: Ambleside, down the hill: the age-restricted strata set for the whole District is Westview Terrace (1390 Duchess Ave), Tudor Gardens (843 22nd St) and Lincoln Gardens (2110 Marine Dr) — all on or near the flat Marine Drive corridor, near the Community Centre, library and Seniors' Activity Centre.
faq.q: Where is the nearest 55+ home I can buy?

faq.a: Also Ambleside: Amica West Vancouver (659 Clyde Ave — the closest, at the Taylor Way end), Hollyburn House (2095 Marine Dr), Kiwanis Manor (959 21st St) and Westerleigh PARC (725 22nd St) for rental retirement living, Amica Lions Gate (701 Keith Rd) on the Park Royal side, and Inglewood Care Centre (725 Inglewood Ave) for publicly funded long-term care. All are rental or care — none is in Whitby Estates and none is strata ownership.
faq.q: Where are the nearest retirement and care options?

faq.a: For a strata unit (Garden Court or Highgrove), long-term rental bans no longer exist in BC — every strata rental-restriction bylaw became invalid on Nov 24, 2022; a strata can still restrict short-term rentals. For a detached house there is no strata at all. If the unit were in an Ambleside 55+ building instead, the tenant would additionally have to satisfy the 55+ age bylaw or an exemption.
faq.q: Can I rent out a home I buy here?

faq.a: The zoning basis exists: the RS single-family zones in Section 200 of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 list secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among permitted uses. Two Whitby Estates overlays still apply on top of zoning — the British Pacific Properties building-scheme plan approval for any new structure, and the District's wildfire/watercourse development permits where they apply.
faq.q: Can I add a suite for a caregiver or family member?

faq.a: Plan on a car. The District's Seniors' Activity Centre in Ambleside runs its own shuttle bus service for seniors — a centre service, not a Whitby Estates bus route.
faq.q: What transit can I actually use day to day?

faq.a: The hospital is Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serving the whole North Shore. The in-District care ladder is entirely in Ambleside: independent 55+ strata and Kiwanis/PARC rental, retirement residences with assisted living (Amica West Vancouver, Hollyburn House, Amica Lions Gate), then Inglewood Care Centre's 230 publicly funded long-term care beds, allocated through Vancouver Coastal Health. Staying in West Vancouver for care means moving down to Ambleside — there is no care option on the British Properties hillside.
